title: Revet: A Language and Compiler for Dataflow Threads
problem: Programming vectorized reconfigurable dataflow accelerators (vRDAs) currently requires either hard-coded kernels or MapReduce-style languages that cannot vectorize data-dependent control flow, limiting their applicability compared to general-purpose CPU/GPU threading models.
motivation: Spatial dataflow architectures provide substantially higher performance and efficiency than CPUs and GPUs, so enabling general-purpose threaded programming on vRDAs would expand application support while maintaining efficiency advantages.
method: Revet provides a threaded programming language designed for vRDAs, paired with an MLIR-based compiler that lowers threaded code to a generic dataflow backend operating on streaming tensors. A specialized execution model efficiently maps threads to dataflow operations, enabling vectorization of data-dependent control flow that prior MapReduce-style approaches could not support.
key_novelty: General-purpose threaded programming model for vectorized dataflow accelerators with compiler and execution engine that efficiently map threaded abstractions to dataflow operations.
contributions: Revet language: threaded programming abstraction for vRDAs supporting broader application classes
MLIR-based compiler lowering threaded code to streaming tensor dataflow operations
Execution model efficiently mapping threaded applications to vectorized dataflow
Achieves 3.8× speedup over GPU-based threaded execution
